title: [R3-4 finding] Real provider process launched with the producer's model/effort argv+env exits 1: foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:837 after 7a227a25
description:
FINDING filed by architect-c1a63707 from task-4cef79f6's final-gate STOP (comment-73740556) at HEAD 24ac4ae9. Owner-less red: the windows suite's authors (task-203a5ca7, task-e7c1875f) are DONE.

MEASURED: before commit 7a227a25 (task-fd196056, DONE) the runner's Windows provider boundary refused the producer's environment (ANTHROPIC_MODEL, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL) at encode, so apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts's real-process arm `observes a real exited provider process and files it in the ledger` failed early (outcome.ok false; suite `3 failed | 5 passed`). After 7a227a25 the environment is admitted, the process RUNS, reaches durable readback, and the arm's `expect(read.record.launch.exit).toMatchObject({ code: 0, kind: "EXITED" })` at :837 fails with `{ kind: "EXITED", code: 1 }` (suite `1 failed | 7 passed`, reproducible in two standalone runs). The arm launches the runtime with argv `["--version", "--model", "claude-opus-5", "--effort", "high"]` (:791) and an environment carrying COMSPEC plus the producer's selection keys (:793-798); its own comment (:776) says this host has no installed claude runtime, so the executable is a stand-in resolved by the runtime pin.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the class of real-process control task-e4cd1eb6's DoD-3 (R3-4) must pass. An exit code of 1 from the launched process means either (a) the stand-in executable rejects the producer's argv/env combination (`--version` with `--model/--effort`, or the env override), (b) the runtime pin resolves to something other than the intended binary once the env is admitted, or (c) the arm's expectation of 0 was only ever reachable because the env was refused. Which one is a measurement, not a guess.

DELIVER: reproduce standalone; attribute the exit code to (a)/(b)/(c) with the exact executable path, argv and env the boundary encoded (read them from the captured launch, never from the test's literals); fix the PRODUCTION defect if (a)/(b) (never edit the arm's expectation to 1), or re-anchor the arm's expectation with a written reason if (c); leave the suite green or with the red disclosed and owned. Consumer: task-e4cd1eb6 (its re-plan's step 5).

FIX per class: (a)/(b) — a production change in the runner or the daemon launch producer (owned paths named at plan time; never the roster widening of task-fd196056 being reverted) with a RED-first arm at the production surface that reproduces exit 1 and goes green; (c) — the arm's expectation is re-anchored ONLY with a written reason in the arm and an assertion that still proves a REAL process ran and exited (kind EXITED, exit code pinned to the measured value, the TELEMETRY_STREAM_ANOMALOUS limit preserved). Never change the arm to `code: 1` without the classification.

The windows suite is green (`Tests 8 passed`) at the delivered commit, or its remaining red is disclosed verbatim with an owner row named; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` (quote `$ tsc`) and, if the runner changed, `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` + `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test` with count lines; path attribution for any other red; explicit-pathspec commit; completion comment names task-e4cd1eb6807244efa3334609ed746143 and task-fd1960561d9b4ba2bbb96ae031ac4606 and states the classification and the exit-code evidence.

Never edit the :837 expectation to match the failure without the (a)/(b)/(c) classification and its evidence; a green suite obtained by asserting the defect is a fabricated pass.
